FEDERAL COMMUNICATIONS COMMISSION WASHINGTON, D.C: 20554
IN REPLY REFER TO:
9400
Honorable Rogers C. B. Morton Secretary, United States Department of the Interior Washington, D. C. 20240
Dear Mr. Secretary:
This concerns the draft environmental statement prepared by the Department of the Interior's Bureau of Outdoor Recreation and dated May 26, 1972. The statement proposes regulations for use of motorized off-road vehicles on the public lands.
The Commission wishes to avail itself of the opportunity extended on June 2, 1972 (37 F.R. 11078) to comment on the draft environmental statement. We are in general agreement with the objectives of the statement which would restrict the use of off-road vehicles on lands administered by the Department to ensure that such use, where permitted, would be compatible with other uses, and would not result in significant adverse environmental impact or cause irreversible damage to existing ecological balances.
The proposed regulations would implement Executive Order 11644 which appears to have been prompted primarily because of the rapidly increasing use of off-road vehicles such as minibikes and snowmobiles for recreational purposes. However, the restrictions appear broad enough to be applicable as well to motorized vehicles used for business or other non-recreational purposes. Accordingly, we are concerned that provision be made so that common carriers and others who have wire, cable or radio communications facilities on public lands pursuant to land-use permits may have reasonable access to such facilities, to whatever extent may be necessary or desirable, in connection with the construction, operation and maintenance of such communications facilities. In this connection, we note that any vehicle whose use was expressly authorized by an agency head of the Department under a permit, lease, license, or contract would be exempt from the proposed use restrictions on off-road vehicles.
